title: Init: introduce installed runtime selection with single-runtime compatibility
description:
## What to build

Split init's current single agent choice into a default scaffold agent and an installed runtime selection, while preserving the current single-runtime behavior when no explicit runtime list is provided. This slice should introduce the runtime data model/registry in the scaffold path and keep the generated config directory coherent for existing one-agent init flows.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] InitService can represent a default scaffold agent separately from installed agent runtimes.
- [ ] Omitting installed runtimes preserves the current behavior by installing the selected default agent runtime.
- [ ] Runtime installation metadata is owned by a runtime registry rather than being coupled to the default scaffold agent entry.
- [ ] The scaffolded `main.mts`/`main.ts` still uses the selected default agent and model for the initial example.
- [ ] Focused InitService tests verify that a single-runtime scaffold remains valid and backward compatible.

None - can start immediately

title: Init: assemble sandbox image from multiple installed runtimes
description:

Generate the sandbox image file by combining install snippets for every selected installed runtime. A project should be able to install, for example, Cursor and Codex in the same Dockerfile or Containerfile without forking templates or emitting unselected runtime setup.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Selecting multiple installed runtimes emits one Dockerfile/Containerfile with all selected runtime CLI install snippets.
- [ ] The generated image file has a single coherent base/system setup and does not duplicate top-level template structure for each runtime.
- [ ] Selecting one runtime still produces a valid simple image for Docker and Podman.
- [ ] Generated image files do not include install snippets for unselected runtimes.
- [ ] Focused scaffold tests cover multiple runtimes, one runtime, Dockerfile output, and Containerfile output.

title: CLI: support interactive and non-interactive runtime selection

- [ ] Interactive init asks for a default agent and then asks which installed runtimes to include, with the default agent runtime selected by default.
- [ ] Non-interactive init accepts a multi-runtime flag, such as `--runtimes codex,cursor`, without requiring prompts.
- [ ] Unknown runtime ids fail before scaffolding or image building starts.

title: Docker build-image should handle UID 0 clearly
description:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** `sandcastle docker build-image` should not fail with a low-level `usermod: UID '0' already exists` error when run as root.

**Source:** Split from #29.

**Current behavior:**

When Sandcastle is run in a WSL2/root environment, `sandcastle docker build-image` may default `AGENT_UID` and `AGENT_GID` from the host process. If the host UID is `0`, the scaffolded Dockerfile can receive `AGENT_UID=0` and then attempt to change the base `node` user to UID 0. That can fail during image build with a low-level error such as `usermod: UID '0' already exists`.

This is confusing because the user is trying to build the standard Sandcastle image, not manually modify Linux users.

**Desired behavior:**

Root/UID 0 should be handled deliberately. The build should either:

- refuse early with a clear Sandcastle error explaining that UID 0 is not a supported default Docker image UID and recommending the WSL/root workaround, or
- choose a safe non-root image UID strategy that avoids `usermod -u 0` and keeps the runtime guidance coherent.

Whichever strategy is chosen, users should not see `usermod: UID '0' already exists` as the primary failure. The message should explain how to proceed, including the relationship between image build UID and `docker({ containerUid, containerGid })` runtime configuration.

**Key interfaces:**

- Docker image build command behavior for default UID/GID build args.
- Generated Dockerfile UID/GID alignment contract for the `agent` user.
- Docker sandbox provider runtime UID/GID options, especially `containerUid` and `containerGid`.
- Documentation for WSL2/root + Docker setup.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] Running the Docker image build path with an effective host UID of 0 no longer reaches a raw `usermod: UID '0' already exists` failure.
- [ ] The chosen behavior has test coverage for UID 0 build-arg/default handling.
- [ ] The user-facing message or generated guidance explains the recommended WSL2/root configuration.
- [ ] Existing non-root UID/GID alignment behavior remains unchanged.
- [ ] The Docker provider still reports UID mismatches clearly when image UID and runtime `containerUid` do not match.

**Out of scope:**

- Changing Podman UID behavior.
- Retrying failed Docker builds.
- Fixing unrelated network failures while downloading agent CLIs.
- Changing GitHub auth or git remote setup behavior.

title: npm exec --yes --package tsx fails when project registry is unavailable (enterprise Artifactory / GFW)
description:
## Environment

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| OS | WSL2 Linux x64 |
| npm registry | Corporate Artifactory (`art-internal.hobot.cc`) configured in `~/.npmrc` |
| Node.js | v20.19.0 |

## Describe the bug

The recommended run command generated by `sandcastle init` (via `InitService.ts`) is:

\`\`\`
npm exec --yes --package tsx -- tsx .sandcastle/main.mts
\`\`\`

When `tsx` is not already cached locally, `npm exec --yes` fetches it **at runtime** from the configured registry. If the registry is unreachable (enterprise Artifactory, GFW, offline/VPN environment), the command fails immediately:

\`\`\`
npm error code ECONNRESET
npm error network request to https://art-internal.hobot.cc/artifactory/api/npm/npm/tsx failed, reason: Client network socket disconnected before secure TLS connection was established
\`\`\`

Sandcastle has no control over this, but the current approach has a silent dependency: **network access to npm at runtime**. The generated `main.mts` comment and `next steps` output both point users to this command without mentioning this caveat.

## Root cause

`InitService.ts` generates `npm exec --yes --package tsx -- tsx .sandcastle/main.mts` as the canonical run command (line 830), but it does **not** add `tsx` as a `devDependency` in the target project's `package.json` during `sandcastle init`. This means `tsx` must be downloaded on demand at every cold start.

## Expected behavior

Either:
1. `sandcastle init` adds `tsx` to `package.json` `devDependencies` alongside `@ai-hero/sandcastle` (so a single `npm install` at setup time is the only network requirement), and the recommended script becomes `npm run sandcastle` using `tsx` from `node_modules/.bin/tsx`
2. Or the `next steps` output warns that the run command requires npm registry access and suggests pre-installing tsx: `npm install --save-dev tsx`

## Workaround

Pre-install tsx locally and run via `npx tsx .sandcastle/main.mts` (using globally cached tsx), or add `tsx` to `devDependencies` manually.

## Related

- `InitService.ts` line 830: `runMainCommand`
- Similar pattern: #33 (codex optional dependency also silently fails under bad network)

title: Dockerfile template: @openai/codex optional platform binary (@openai/codex-linux-x64) silently missing after npm install -g
description:
## Environment

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| OS | WSL2 (Linux x64) |
| Sandcastle | latest (`file:../sandcastle`) |
| Docker image | `sandcastle:drobotics_tools` |
| Codex version in image | 0.133.0 |

## Describe the bug

When running `npx tsx ./.sandcastle/main.mts`, the planner exits immediately with:

\`\`\`
AgentError: codex exited with code 1:
Error: Missing optional dependency @openai/codex-linux-x64.
Reinstall Codex: npm install -g @openai/codex@latest
\`\`\`

The Dockerfile template generated by `sandcastle init` (from `src/InitService.ts`) contains:

\`\`\`dockerfile
# Install Codex CLI (run as root before USER agent)
RUN npm install -g @openai/codex
\`\`\`

`@openai/codex` ships a platform-specific native binary as an **optional dependency** (e.g. `@openai/codex-linux-x64`). When npm fails to download an optional dependency (due to network/proxy instability — common in mainland China), it **silently skips** it and still exits 0. The image builds successfully, but `codex` crashes at runtime.

Verified in the built image:

\`\`\`
$ docker run --rm ... bash -lc 'codex --version'
Error: Missing optional dependency @openai/codex-linux-x64. Reinstall Codex: npm install -g @openai/codex@latest

$ docker run --rm ... bash -lc 'npm ls -g @openai/codex @openai/codex-linux-x64'
/usr/local/lib
└── @openai/codex@0.133.0
# @openai/codex-linux-x64 is absent
\`\`\`

## Root cause

`npm install -g @openai/codex` can produce an incomplete installation when the optional platform binary download fails. There is no post-install validation in the Dockerfile template.

## Expected behavior

The generated Dockerfile should guarantee that `codex` is runnable inside the container. Either:
1. Explicitly install the platform binary: `RUN npm install -g @openai/codex @openai/codex-linux-x64` (on linux/amd64)
2. Or add a verification step after install: `RUN codex --version` so the build **fails fast** if the binary is missing, rather than succeeding silently and crashing at agent runtime.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `sandcastle init` with Codex agent on a Linux x64 host with unstable npm access (proxy / GFW)
2. `sandcastle docker build-image` — build succeeds
3. `npx tsx .sandcastle/main.mts` — planner fails immediately with the error above

## Related

- #29 Bug 4 mentions Cursor CLI download timeout in similar network conditions; this is the Codex equivalent.

title: sandcastle init does not create package.json or install @ai-hero/sandcastle in target project, causing ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on first run
description:
## Environment

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| OS | WSL2 Linux x64 |
| Node.js | v20.19.0 |
| Sandcastle | 0.5.9 (file:../sandcastle) |

## Describe the bug

When `sandcastle init` is run in a project that **has no `package.json`**, it scaffolds `.sandcastle/` but does not create a `package.json` or install `@ai-hero/sandcastle`. Running `main.mts` then fails immediately:

\`\`\`
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package '@ai-hero/sandcastle'
imported from /path/to/project/.sandcastle/main.mts
\`\`\`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new directory (Python project, or any non-Node project without an existing `package.json`)
2. `sandcastle init` — completes successfully, scaffolds `.sandcastle/`
3. `npx tsx .sandcastle/main.mts` → **ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND**

The user must manually run `npm install --save-dev @ai-hero/sandcastle` (or `npm link @ai-hero/sandcastle` for local dev) before `main.mts` can be imported. The generated next-steps output mentions this step but does not enforce or automate it.

## Root cause

`InitService.ts` scaffolds `main.mts` with `import * as sandcastle from "@ai-hero/sandcastle"` but does not write or update a `package.json` in the project root. Node ESM module resolution requires `@ai-hero/sandcastle` to exist in `node_modules/` relative to the script — without a `package.json` + `npm install`, there is no `node_modules/`.

The "next steps" output includes:

> Add `"sandcastle": "npm exec --yes --package tsx -- tsx .sandcastle/main.mts"` to your package.json scripts

But if there is no `package.json`, the user has to create one first, and there is no clear guidance for non-Node (e.g. Python) projects.

## Expected behavior

`sandcastle init` should either:
1. **Create or update `package.json`** in the project root with `@ai-hero/sandcastle` and `tsx` as `devDependencies`, and run `npm install`
2. Or at minimum **detect the absence of `package.json`** and print an explicit error or prompt: `No package.json found. Run \`npm init -y && npm install --save-dev @ai-hero/sandcastle tsx\` first.`

This is especially important for **non-Node projects** (Python, C++, etc.) which are a stated use case of Sandcastle but have no `package.json` by default.

## Observed workaround

User ran `npm link @ai-hero/sandcastle` to create a symlink, which resolved the import. Correct fix is `npm install --save-dev @ai-hero/sandcastle` with a `package.json`.

## Related

- #34 — tsx also needs to be a devDependency for offline/enterprise-registry scenarios
- #29 Bug field report (WSL2 root init issues)

title: Planner prompt expansion: opaque 401 when Docker sandbox gh token in .sandcastle/auth/gh is invalid
description:
## Summary

Running `parallel-planner-with-review` (`.sandcastle/main.ts`) fails during **Phase 1 (planner)** before the agent starts, with a `PromptError` from `PromptPreprocessor` when expanding the `!`gh issue list ...`` shell block in `.sandcastle/plan-prompt.md`.

The underlying failure is GitHub API **401 Unauthorized** (`Bad credentials`), but the run exits as an uncaught Effect fiber failure with a long stack trace rather than a short, actionable auth message.

## Environment

- Template: `parallel-planner-with-review`
- Sandbox: `docker()` with mount `.sandcastle/auth/gh` → `/home/agent/.config/gh`
- Host `gh auth status`: logged in via system keyring
- Project gh config: `GH_CONFIG_DIR=.sandcastle/auth/gh gh auth status` → **token in hosts.yml is invalid**
- `.sandcastle/.env`: `GH_TOKEN=` empty (skipped by `resolveEnv`, so no override)

## Reproduction

1. Scaffold/init with GitHub Issues backlog manager (generates `plan-prompt.md` with `gh issue list -l Sandcastle ...`).
2. Run `gh auth login` into `.sandcastle/auth/gh` once, then let the stored oauth token expire or revoke it (or use a stale `hosts.yml`).
3. Ensure host `gh` still works (keyring) but project config does not:
   ```bash
   gh auth status   # OK
   GH_CONFIG_DIR=.sandcastle/auth/gh gh auth status   # invalid token
   ```
4. Run:
   ```bash
   npm exec --yes --package tsx -- tsx .sandcastle/main.ts
   ```
5. Observe crash on iteration 1 planner with `PromptError` / 401 from `gh issue list`.

## Expected behavior

- Fail fast with a clear message, e.g.:
  - invalid/expired `.sandcastle/auth/gh` credentials, or
  - missing `GH_TOKEN` when using GitHub Issues templates in Docker, with pointers to:
    - `GH_CONFIG_DIR=.sandcastle/auth/gh gh auth login --insecure-storage`
    - or set `GH_TOKEN` in `.sandcastle/.env`
- Optional: preflight in `run()` / init docs when `github-issues` backlog is selected.

## Actual behavior

- `preprocessPrompt` runs `gh issue list` inside the Docker sandbox using mounted `.sandcastle/auth/gh`.
- `gh` returns 401; Sandcastle throws `PromptError` and the Node process terminates with a full fiber stack trace.

## Notes

- This is primarily a **DX / diagnostics** issue: configuration is wrong, but host and sandbox auth are easy to confuse because host `gh` can work while sandbox `gh` does not.
- `resolveEnv` intentionally omits empty `GH_TOKEN=`; users may believe `.env` is “set up” when it is not.

## Suggested implementation directions

1. Detect `gh` auth failure stderr (`401`, `Bad credentials`, `token ... is invalid`) in prompt expansion and wrap with setup hints (link README / `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`).
2. Optional preflight before planner when prompt contains `gh issue list` and sandbox mounts `auth/gh`.
3. Document in README / init output that **host** `gh auth status` success does not imply **sandbox** auth success.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Repro above surfaces a single actionable error (no deep Effect stack as the primary signal).
- [ ] Message mentions both remediation paths (`GH_TOKEN` and `GH_CONFIG_DIR=.sandcastle/auth/gh gh auth login`).
- [ ] Regression test or doc update as appropriate.

title: Agent auth failures should guide users to sandcastle env commands, not agent login
description:
## Problem

When Hub flows such as `sandcastle tasks from-prd` fail because Cursor (or other agent) auth is missing, users see the raw agent CLI message:

> Please run `agent login` first, or set `CURSOR_API_KEY`

That message does not match how Sandcastle expects credentials to be configured. Users should be steered toward Sandcastle guidance such as `sandcastle env init` and `sandcastle env set` instead.

## Root cause

`Orchestrator.formatNonZeroExitDetail` passes through raw `stderr` / `resultText` without remediation. GitHub `gh` auth failures are already handled with better guidance in `PromptPreprocessor`; agent auth failures are not.

## Proposed fix (scope)

**In scope:**

- Add a new `agentAuthGuidance` module to detect agent auth failures and format Sandcastle-specific remediation text.
- Integrate guidance in `Orchestrator.invokeAgent`.
- Add Hub preflight checks in `hubProposalAgent` and `hubFlowExecution` (`runHubAgent`).
- Cover behavior with tests (TDD).

**Explicitly out of scope:**

- Changing the `sandcastle init` auth setup flow in `cli.ts`.

## Affected surfaces

- `sandcastle tasks from-prd` / triage Hub flows
- Hub `run` flows
- Project `run()` / `interactive()`
- Similar auth errors from Codex, Pi, Claude, and other providers

## Acceptance criteria

- On missing or invalid agent auth, error output mentions `sandcastle env init` / `sandcastle env set` (or equivalent documented Sandcastle env workflow), not only `agent login` / raw env var names without Sandcastle context.
- Behavior is consistent for Orchestrator-invoked agents and Hub preflight paths.
- Tests assert detection and formatted remediation for representative auth failure messages.

title: Docker build-image should handle UID 0 clearly
description:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** bug
**Summary:** `sandcastle docker build-image` should not fail with a low-level `usermod: UID '0' already exists` error when run as root.

**Source:** Split from #29.

**Current behavior:**

When Sandcastle is run in a WSL2/root environment, `sandcastle docker build-image` may default `AGENT_UID` and `AGENT_GID` from the host process. If the host UID is `0`, the scaffolded Dockerfile can receive `AGENT_UID=0` and then attempt to change the base `node` user to UID 0. That can fail during image build with a low-level error such as `usermod: UID '0' already exists`.

This is confusing because the user is trying to build the standard Sandcastle image, not manually modify Linux users.

**Desired behavior:**

Root/UID 0 should be handled deliberately. The build should either:

- refuse early with a clear Sandcastle error explaining that UID 0 is not a supported default Docker image UID and recommending the WSL/root workaround, or
- choose a safe non-root image UID strategy that avoids `usermod -u 0` and keeps the runtime guidance coherent.

Whichever strategy is chosen, users should not see `usermod: UID '0' already exists` as the primary failure. The message should explain how to proceed, including the relationship between image build UID and `docker({ containerUid, containerGid })` runtime configuration.

**Key interfaces:**

- Docker image build command behavior for default UID/GID build args.
- Generated Dockerfile UID/GID alignment contract for the `agent` user.
- Docker sandbox provider runtime UID/GID options, especially `containerUid` and `containerGid`.
- Documentation for WSL2/root + Docker setup.

**Acceptance criteria:**

- [ ] Running the Docker image build path with an effective host UID of 0 no longer reaches a raw `usermod: UID '0' already exists` failure.
- [ ] The chosen behavior has test coverage for UID 0 build-arg/default handling.
- [ ] The user-facing message or generated guidance explains the recommended WSL2/root configuration.
- [ ] Existing non-root UID/GID alignment behavior remains unchanged.
- [ ] The Docker provider still reports UID mismatches clearly when image UID and runtime `containerUid` do not match.

**Out of scope:**

- Changing Podman UID behavior.
- Retrying failed Docker builds.
- Fixing unrelated network failures while downloading agent CLIs.
- Changing GitHub auth or git remote setup behavior.

title: Dockerfile template: @openai/codex optional platform binary (@openai/codex-linux-x64) silently missing after npm install -g
description:
## Environment

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| OS | WSL2 (Linux x64) |
| Sandcastle | latest (`file:../sandcastle`) |
| Docker image | `sandcastle:drobotics_tools` |
| Codex version in image | 0.133.0 |

## Describe the bug

When running `npx tsx ./.sandcastle/main.mts`, the planner exits immediately with:

\`\`\`
AgentError: codex exited with code 1:
Error: Missing optional dependency @openai/codex-linux-x64.
Reinstall Codex: npm install -g @openai/codex@latest
\`\`\`

The Dockerfile template generated by `sandcastle init` (from `src/InitService.ts`) contains:

\`\`\`dockerfile
# Install Codex CLI (run as root before USER agent)
RUN npm install -g @openai/codex
\`\`\`

`@openai/codex` ships a platform-specific native binary as an **optional dependency** (e.g. `@openai/codex-linux-x64`). When npm fails to download an optional dependency (due to network/proxy instability — common in mainland China), it **silently skips** it and still exits 0. The image builds successfully, but `codex` crashes at runtime.

Verified in the built image:

\`\`\`
$ docker run --rm ... bash -lc 'codex --version'
Error: Missing optional dependency @openai/codex-linux-x64. Reinstall Codex: npm install -g @openai/codex@latest

$ docker run --rm ... bash -lc 'npm ls -g @openai/codex @openai/codex-linux-x64'
/usr/local/lib
└── @openai/codex@0.133.0
# @openai/codex-linux-x64 is absent
\`\`\`

## Root cause

`npm install -g @openai/codex` can produce an incomplete installation when the optional platform binary download fails. There is no post-install validation in the Dockerfile template.

## Expected behavior

The generated Dockerfile should guarantee that `codex` is runnable inside the container. Either:
1. Explicitly install the platform binary: `RUN npm install -g @openai/codex @openai/codex-linux-x64` (on linux/amd64)
2. Or add a verification step after install: `RUN codex --version` so the build **fails fast** if the binary is missing, rather than succeeding silently and crashing at agent runtime.

## Steps to reproduce

1. `sandcastle init` with Codex agent on a Linux x64 host with unstable npm access (proxy / GFW)
2. `sandcastle docker build-image` — build succeeds
3. `npx tsx .sandcastle/main.mts` — planner fails immediately with the error above

## Related

- #29 Bug 4 mentions Cursor CLI download timeout in similar network conditions; this is the Codex equivalent.

title: sandcastle init does not create package.json or install @ai-hero/sandcastle in target project, causing ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on first run
description:
## Environment

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| OS | WSL2 Linux x64 |
| Node.js | v20.19.0 |
| Sandcastle | 0.5.9 (file:../sandcastle) |

## Describe the bug

When `sandcastle init` is run in a project that **has no `package.json`**, it scaffolds `.sandcastle/` but does not create a `package.json` or install `@ai-hero/sandcastle`. Running `main.mts` then fails immediately:

\`\`\`
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package '@ai-hero/sandcastle'
imported from /path/to/project/.sandcastle/main.mts
\`\`\`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new directory (Python project, or any non-Node project without an existing `package.json`)
2. `sandcastle init` — completes successfully, scaffolds `.sandcastle/`
3. `npx tsx .sandcastle/main.mts` → **ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND**

The user must manually run `npm install --save-dev @ai-hero/sandcastle` (or `npm link @ai-hero/sandcastle` for local dev) before `main.mts` can be imported. The generated next-steps output mentions this step but does not enforce or automate it.

## Root cause

`InitService.ts` scaffolds `main.mts` with `import * as sandcastle from "@ai-hero/sandcastle"` but does not write or update a `package.json` in the project root. Node ESM module resolution requires `@ai-hero/sandcastle` to exist in `node_modules/` relative to the script — without a `package.json` + `npm install`, there is no `node_modules/`.

The "next steps" output includes:

> Add `"sandcastle": "npm exec --yes --package tsx -- tsx .sandcastle/main.mts"` to your package.json scripts

But if there is no `package.json`, the user has to create one first, and there is no clear guidance for non-Node (e.g. Python) projects.

## Expected behavior

`sandcastle init` should either:
1. **Create or update `package.json`** in the project root with `@ai-hero/sandcastle` and `tsx` as `devDependencies`, and run `npm install`
2. Or at minimum **detect the absence of `package.json`** and print an explicit error or prompt: `No package.json found. Run \`npm init -y && npm install --save-dev @ai-hero/sandcastle tsx\` first.`

This is especially important for **non-Node projects** (Python, C++, etc.) which are a stated use case of Sandcastle but have no `package.json` by default.

## Observed workaround

User ran `npm link @ai-hero/sandcastle` to create a symlink, which resolved the import. Correct fix is `npm install --save-dev @ai-hero/sandcastle` with a `package.json`.

## Related

- #34 — tsx also needs to be a devDependency for offline/enterprise-registry scenarios
- #29 Bug field report (WSL2 root init issues)

title: npm exec --yes --package tsx fails when project registry is unavailable (enterprise Artifactory / GFW)
description:
## Environment

| Item | Value |
|------|-------|
| OS | WSL2 Linux x64 |
| npm registry | Corporate Artifactory (`art-internal.hobot.cc`) configured in `~/.npmrc` |
| Node.js | v20.19.0 |

## Describe the bug

The recommended run command generated by `sandcastle init` (via `InitService.ts`) is:

\`\`\`
npm exec --yes --package tsx -- tsx .sandcastle/main.mts
\`\`\`

When `tsx` is not already cached locally, `npm exec --yes` fetches it **at runtime** from the configured registry. If the registry is unreachable (enterprise Artifactory, GFW, offline/VPN environment), the command fails immediately:

\`\`\`
npm error code ECONNRESET
npm error network request to https://art-internal.hobot.cc/artifactory/api/npm/npm/tsx failed, reason: Client network socket disconnected before secure TLS connection was established
\`\`\`

Sandcastle has no control over this, but the current approach has a silent dependency: **network access to npm at runtime**. The generated `main.mts` comment and `next steps` output both point users to this command without mentioning this caveat.

## Root cause

`InitService.ts` generates `npm exec --yes --package tsx -- tsx .sandcastle/main.mts` as the canonical run command (line 830), but it does **not** add `tsx` as a `devDependency` in the target project's `package.json` during `sandcastle init`. This means `tsx` must be downloaded on demand at every cold start.

## Expected behavior

Either:
1. `sandcastle init` adds `tsx` to `package.json` `devDependencies` alongside `@ai-hero/sandcastle` (so a single `npm install` at setup time is the only network requirement), and the recommended script becomes `npm run sandcastle` using `tsx` from `node_modules/.bin/tsx`
2. Or the `next steps` output warns that the run command requires npm registry access and suggests pre-installing tsx: `npm install --save-dev tsx`

## Workaround

Pre-install tsx locally and run via `npx tsx .sandcastle/main.mts` (using globally cached tsx), or add `tsx` to `devDependencies` manually.

## Related

- `InitService.ts` line 830: `runMainCommand`
- Similar pattern: #33 (codex optional dependency also silently fails under bad network)

title: Planner prompt expansion: opaque 401 when Docker sandbox gh token in .sandcastle/auth/gh is invalid
description:
## Summary

Running `parallel-planner-with-review` (`.sandcastle/main.ts`) fails during **Phase 1 (planner)** before the agent starts, with a `PromptError` from `PromptPreprocessor` when expanding the `!`gh issue list ...`` shell block in `.sandcastle/plan-prompt.md`.

The underlying failure is GitHub API **401 Unauthorized** (`Bad credentials`), but the run exits as an uncaught Effect fiber failure with a long stack trace rather than a short, actionable auth message.

## Environment

- Template: `parallel-planner-with-review`
- Sandbox: `docker()` with mount `.sandcastle/auth/gh` → `/home/agent/.config/gh`
- Host `gh auth status`: logged in via system keyring
- Project gh config: `GH_CONFIG_DIR=.sandcastle/auth/gh gh auth status` → **token in hosts.yml is invalid**
- `.sandcastle/.env`: `GH_TOKEN=` empty (skipped by `resolveEnv`, so no override)

## Reproduction

1. Scaffold/init with GitHub Issues backlog manager (generates `plan-prompt.md` with `gh issue list -l Sandcastle ...`).
2. Run `gh auth login` into `.sandcastle/auth/gh` once, then let the stored oauth token expire or revoke it (or use a stale `hosts.yml`).
3. Ensure host `gh` still works (keyring) but project config does not:
   ```bash
   gh auth status   # OK
   GH_CONFIG_DIR=.sandcastle/auth/gh gh auth status   # invalid token
   ```
4. Run:
   ```bash
   npm exec --yes --package tsx -- tsx .sandcastle/main.ts
   ```
5. Observe crash on iteration 1 planner with `PromptError` / 401 from `gh issue list`.

## Expected behavior

- Fail fast with a clear message, e.g.:
  - invalid/expired `.sandcastle/auth/gh` credentials, or
  - missing `GH_TOKEN` when using GitHub Issues templates in Docker, with pointers to:
    - `GH_CONFIG_DIR=.sandcastle/auth/gh gh auth login --insecure-storage`
    - or set `GH_TOKEN` in `.sandcastle/.env`
- Optional: preflight in `run()` / init docs when `github-issues` backlog is selected.

## Actual behavior

- `preprocessPrompt` runs `gh issue list` inside the Docker sandbox using mounted `.sandcastle/auth/gh`.
- `gh` returns 401; Sandcastle throws `PromptError` and the Node process terminates with a full fiber stack trace.

## Notes

- This is primarily a **DX / diagnostics** issue: configuration is wrong, but host and sandbox auth are easy to confuse because host `gh` can work while sandbox `gh` does not.
- `resolveEnv` intentionally omits empty `GH_TOKEN=`; users may believe `.env` is “set up” when it is not.

## Suggested implementation directions

1. Detect `gh` auth failure stderr (`401`, `Bad credentials`, `token ... is invalid`) in prompt expansion and wrap with setup hints (link README / `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`).
2. Optional preflight before planner when prompt contains `gh issue list` and sandbox mounts `auth/gh`.
3. Document in README / init output that **host** `gh auth status` success does not imply **sandbox** auth success.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Repro above surfaces a single actionable error (no deep Effect stack as the primary signal).
- [ ] Message mentions both remediation paths (`GH_TOKEN` and `GH_CONFIG_DIR=.sandcastle/auth/gh gh auth login`).
- [ ] Regression test or doc update as appropriate.

title: Agent auth failures should guide users to sandcastle env commands, not agent login
description:

> Please run `agent login` first, or set `CURSOR_API_KEY`

That message does not match how Sandcastle expects credentials to be configured. Users should be steered toward Sandcastle guidance such as `sandcastle env init` and `sandcastle env set` instead.

`Orchestrator.formatNonZeroExitDetail` passes through raw `stderr` / `resultText` without remediation. GitHub `gh` auth failures are already handled with better guidance in `PromptPreprocessor`; agent auth failures are not.

**In scope:**

- Add a new `agentAuthGuidance` module to detect agent auth failures and format Sandcastle-specific remediation text.
- Integrate guidance in `Orchestrator.invokeAgent`.
- Add Hub preflight checks in `hubProposalAgent` and `hubFlowExecution` (`runHubAgent`).
- Cover behavior with tests (TDD).

**Explicitly out of scope:**

- Changing the `sandcastle init` auth setup flow in `cli.ts`.

- `sandcastle tasks from-prd` / triage Hub flows
- Hub `run` flows
- Project `run()` / `interactive()`
- Similar auth errors from Codex, Pi, Claude, and other providers

## Acceptance criteria

- On missing or invalid agent auth, error output mentions `sandcastle env init` / `sandcastle env set` (or equivalent documented Sandcastle env workflow), not only `agent login` / raw env var names without Sandcastle context.
- Behavior is consistent for Orchestrator-invoked agents and Hub preflight paths.

title: Agent auth failures should guide users to sandcastle env commands, not agent login
description:
## Problem

When Hub flows such as `sandcastle tasks from-prd` fail because Cursor (or other agent) auth is missing, users see the raw agent CLI message:

> Please run `agent login` first, or set `CURSOR_API_KEY`

That message does not match how Sandcastle expects credentials to be configured. Users should be steered toward Sandcastle guidance such as `sandcastle env init` and `sandcastle env set` instead.

## Root cause

`Orchestrator.formatNonZeroExitDetail` passes through raw `stderr` / `resultText` without remediation. GitHub `gh` auth failures are already handled with better guidance in `PromptPreprocessor`; agent auth failures are not.

## Proposed fix (scope)

**In scope:**

- Add a new `agentAuthGuidance` module to detect agent auth failures and format Sandcastle-specific remediation text.
- Integrate guidance in `Orchestrator.invokeAgent`.
- Add Hub preflight checks in `hubProposalAgent` and `hubFlowExecution` (`runHubAgent`).
- Cover behavior with tests (TDD).

**Explicitly out of scope:**

- Changing the `sandcastle init` auth setup flow in `cli.ts`.

## Affected surfaces

- `sandcastle tasks from-prd` / triage Hub flows
- Hub `run` flows
- Project `run()` / `interactive()`
- Similar auth errors from Codex, Pi, Claude, and other providers

## Acceptance criteria

- On missing or invalid agent auth, error output mentions `sandcastle env init` / `sandcastle env set` (or equivalent documented Sandcastle env workflow), not only `agent login` / raw env var names without Sandcastle context.
- Behavior is consistent for Orchestrator-invoked agents and Hub preflight paths.
- Tests assert detection and formatted remediation for representative auth failure messages.
